units.translation: The Nile was formerly called Triton. It was renamed after Neilos, the Cyclops, son of Tantalus, who was king of the country, as Hermippus (fr. 77 M. III 53) says.

b. Rain in abundance: ambiguity in the construction. For it means either "they sprout in abundance" or "rain does not wet abundantly," since it does not rain continuously in Egypt.

272-74. From there indeed some: Sesonchosis, king of all Egypt after Horus, the son of Isis and Osiris, set out and subdued all Asia, and likewise most of Europe. More accurate accounts about him are in Herodotus (II 102-10). Theopompus in the third book (115 fr. 46 J.) calls him Sesostris. Herodotus adds (102) that if he subdued any peoples in war, he set up pillars recording how he conquered; but if they yielded, he added to the pillars a female genital as a symbol of their softness. Or even not; for abundant enough: For either some of the cities have been abandoned and, having been renamed, are unknown, by whom they happen to have been founded; and time has been the cause of this. Concerning the times in which Sesonchosis lived, Apollonius says "for abundant enough time has passed," but Dicaearchus in the first book (see sch. 272/74) says that Sesonchosis was king after Horus, the son of Isis and Osiris. From Sesonchosis to the reign of Neilos is 2,500 years, <from the reign of Neilos to the capture of Troy 7,> from the capture of Troy to the first Olympiad 433, in total 2,943.
